# Independent JCS vectors

`jcs-numbers.json` records literal IEEE-754 bit patterns and expected JSON spellings
from RFC 8785 Appendix B, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.html#appendix-B
(Anders Rundgren, Brett Jordan and Samuel Erdtman, June 2020). These values are
also cross-checked against the reference samples shipped in the reviewed
`rfc8785` 0.1.4 sdist; expected bytes are committed literals, never generated by
Lotuspond or by the canonicalizer under test. Null expectations represent
nonfinite inputs that JCS must refuse. RFC section 3.2.2's complete value sample
and section 3.2.3's UTF-16 ordering are pinned in `test_canonical.py`.

`scripts/checks/jcs-oracle.mjs` independently uses Node's native scalar
`JSON.stringify`, sorts strings by UTF-16 units and directly assembles object
members (so integer-like property names retain the required lexical order).
It imports no Python/JCS code and is not an SDK runtime dependency.

The inspected PyPI `rfc8785-0.1.4.tar.gz` SHA-256 is
`e545841329fe0eee4f6a3b44e7034343100c12b4ec566dc06ca9735681deb4da`.
The Trail of Bits implementation has no runtime dependencies and is distributed
under Apache-2.0, including its attributed reference float/string serializer.
Lotuspond calls the library; it does not copy its implementation.
